issues.description: The problem statement and UML specify a Rideable interface (with messageOnRide()) and the template/Main refers to Rideable, but the solution repository does not provide a proper Rideable implementation. Instead the solution introduces a different interface named Mountable (with messageOnRide()) and leaves Rideable.java effectively empty. This name/type mismatch between Rideable and Mountable is a structural inconsistency that will confuse students: they are instructed to implement/use Rideable, the template/Main references Rideable, but the provided solution uses Mountable. Students may be blocked or misled when comparing their implementation to the solution or tests that expect Rideable to exist and be implemented by Pig and Seal.
issues.suggestedFix: Make the interface name consistent across all artifacts. Either (A) rename Mountable.java to Rideable.java (and ensure it declares messageOnRide()) and have Pig and Seal implement Rideable, or (B) update the problem statement and template to refer to Mountable instead of Rideable. Ensure Rideable.java in the solution is not empty and that Pig and Seal implement the interface named in the specification/template.

issues.description: The problem statement and template refer to an interface named 'Rideable' (with method messageOnRide()), but the solution implementation introduces a different interface name 'Mountable' and leaves Rideable.java empty. This mismatched identifier for the same conceptual entity (the rideable interface) creates confusion: students reading the problem and template will look for/implement 'Rideable', while the solution's classes implement 'Mountable', breaking the direct mapping between requirement and implementation.
issues.suggestedFix: Use a single consistent interface name across all artifacts. Prefer renaming 'Mountable' in the solution to 'Rideable' (and ensure Rideable.java defines String messageOnRide()), and update all implementing classes to implement Rideable. Alternatively, if 'Mountable' is preferred, update the problem statement and template to use 'Mountable' instead; however, aligning to 'Rideable' preserves the original problem wording.
